findings: Per-shell weight solving eliminates pinching completely — 0 collapsed, 0 inverted, 0 torn faces at every bend angle tested.
Every static asset in the corpus rigs: 9 of 9, no refusals, no errors. The multi-primitive limit never bit — the whole corpus is single-primitive.

The collision metric was wrong and got fixed. Counting any new bounding-box contact reported 334 'collisions' on gasket at 45 degrees; measuring overlap depth shows a median of 8% of a part's volume. That is articulation, not clipping. The real interpenetration count is 28.

Grouping touching shells was the obvious fix and it fails: union-find is transitive, so any epsilon above zero collapsed all 395 shells into one group — and clipping did not improve even then. Kept as a documented negative result, disabled by default.
The corpus's fragmentation scale (~0.18 on gasket's axis) bounds useful bone density. Below it, skinning degenerates to rigid part binding.
